question: Do older official flood advisories or other source-named local waterways explain whether “Silongin Lagda” is the EMB-listed Silongin River?
purpose: Check historical source-name recurrence and nearby named-waterway context without merging distinct names on locality alone.

findings.evidence: Quezon General Flood Advisory No. 1 issued 9 December 2022 directly lists “Silongin Lagda” among Quezon watercourses likely to be affected.
supports: official historical use of the exact compound label in 2022
doesNotSupport: whether the phrase names one or multiple features
a link to EMB Silongin River

findings.evidence: Quezon General Flood Advisory No. 14 issued 7 August 2026 again lists “Silongin Lagda.” The notice is historical and time-bounded.
supports: official recurrence of the compound label in a separate 2026 advisory
doesNotSupport: a verified river route or current flood status

findings.evidence: An official-domain search result for NDRRMC’s 24 December 2018 advisory snippet also displayed “Silongin Lagda” in the Quezon list; direct PDF retrieval returned HTTP 403, so this remains an unverified retrieval lead rather than verified full-text evidence.
supports: a lead suggesting the phrase may predate the directly reviewed 2022 advisory
doesNotSupport: verified full contents of the 2018 PDF

findings.evidence: DENR-EMB Table 3.3 names “Silongin River” under San Francisco, Quezon and reports historical B/C classification for 2019; it does not include “Lagda.”
doesNotSupport: a match to the whole “Silongin Lagda” label
current water quality, geometry, or fish presence

findings.evidence: The Quezon provincial directory lists Silongin as a barangay in San Francisco, which supplies locality context only.
doesNotSupport: river identity, the “Lagda” component, or a route

additionalSearchLead.description: A web search surfaced a DPWH-styled detailed engineering design plan titled for Kanguinsa River, Barangay Silongin, San Francisco, on a third-party Scribd upload. The apparent chainage runs roughly 8+955 to 9+241.60, but the project file was not retrieved from an official DPWH source; authenticity, complete technical context, and reuse terms were not verified.
additionalSearchLead.disposition: Not admitted as a source record or geometry. It does not explain “Lagda” and does not establish that Kanguinsa River is the EMB-listed Silongin River.

crosswalk.resolutionLevel: historical label recurrence only; advisory-to-river link remains unresolved
crosswalk.mergeDecision: Keep the advisory label out of the Silongin River lead and do not add “Lagda” or “Kanguinsa” as an alias. Obtain an official explanation or primary route document before any merge.

nextActions: Request an accessible official copy of the NDRRMC 2018 advisory and the DPWH Quezon III DEO Kanguinsa project design or route sheet.
Ask an authoritative Quezon/municipal source whether “Silongin Lagda” refers to Silongin River, Kanguinsa River, or a separate reach; keep the names distinct until answered.
Search dated, station-resolved fish surveys for the confirmed Silongin/Kanguinsa features as separate leads; do not infer absence from search non-results.
nonClaims: Repeated historical flood-advisory wording is not proof of a single river, a standardized name, or present flood risk.
The third-party Kanguinsa design-plan upload is a discovery lead only; no coordinates, route geometry, or dimensions were imported.
No fish species, current presence/absence, water quality, access, fishing rule, diet, or public app entry is established.
